@@70242570 <h> Devonian integrative stratigraphy and timescale of China <p> The Devonian ( 419.2-358.9 Ma ) is the first geological period of the late Paleozoic , spanning about 60.3 Ma from the end of the Silurian , and its beginning is marked by the First Appearance Datum ( FAD ) of graptolite Uncinatograptus uniformis . During this time interval , the Earth ? s climate system underwent severe perturbations , characterized by drastic dropdown of atmospheric CO2 concentration , and gradual transition from the Silurian ' greenhouse ' Earth to the Permo-Carboniferous ' icehouse ' Earth . The complex pattern of Devonian climate change were controlled by multiple factors at different time scales , and induced 25 global events that are characterized by sea-level rise and fall , ocean anoxic/hypoxic events , and/or biological extinctions/turnovers . Establishment of high-resolution Devonian integrative stratigraphy and timescale framework is essential for the studies on the complex ocean-land-atmosphere interactions during Devonian at different temporal and spatial scales . <p> A review paper by Qie et al . ( 2018 ) was published recently in Science China : Earth Sciences . Based on well-studied bio- and chronostratigraphy of Devonian in South China and adjacent areas @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , event stratigraphy and radioactive isotope ages , this paper and briefly summarize the research history and current status of Devonian chronostratigraphy of China , and for the first time introduce Devonian integrative stratigraphy framework of China . <p> In 1985 , the global Devonian chronostratigraphy scale was formally defined and subdivided into three series , the lower , middle and upper , and contains seven global stages . Till 1996 , all seven Devonian stages ' GSSPs have been formally defined and ratified . Conodont is a key taxon in the Devonian biostratigraphic research . 6 out of the 7 global stages of Devonian , except for the basal Devonian boundary , are marked by the FAD of certain conodont species . By summarizing the taxonomy and biostratigraphy of conodonts in China , Wang ( 2018 ) confirmed 58 Devonian conodonts zones in pelagic facies , among which the biozones of Emsian to Famennian can be precisely correlated to the standard international conodont zones . The bases of the Emsian and the Devonian-Carboniferous boundary ( DCB ) has been defined by the FAD of conodont Polygnathus kitabicus and Siphonodella @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the bases of the Emsian and DCB have received major criticism since the very beginning of their ratification , and in 2008 , the Subcommission on Devonian Stratigraphy ( SDS ) and Subcommisson on Carboniferous Stratigraphy ( SCCS ) have decided to redefine the boundary criteria and levels , which are still ongoing investigations . In addition to conodont biostratigraphy , important progresses on biostratigraphic research of graptolite , ostracods , brachiopods , rugose corals , as well as spores and plants are emphatically introduced in this paper . <p> As for chemostratigraphy , carbon and strontium isotopic records from South China show similar trend with Euramerica sections , and have global correlation significances. d13C values show major positive shifts in the Silurian-Devonian boundary , Kac ? k , Frasne , lower and upper Kellwasser , as well as Hangenberg events , suggesting global carbon cycle perturbation during these critical time intervals . In Longmenshan region , 87Sr/86Sr values are 0.70788-0.70868 , and its long-term trend agrees with a published mean LOWESS fitted line . After a gradual decline from early Devonian , 87Sr/86Sr ratios reach nadir values and stay @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Frasnian and define a plateau throughout the Famennian. 87Sr/86Sr ratios can be used as a tool for precise stratigraphic correlation and dating . This paper also give a detail introduction about Devonian event stratigraphy , cyclostratigraphy , geological chronology , and stratigraphic correlation among main major palaeobiogeography realms in China . <p> At present , the main tasks for the researches on Devonian of China include : 1 ) establishment of continuous astronomical time scale and high-resolution radioactive isotope dating ; 2 ) further subdivision of Chinese regional chronostratigraphy ; 3 ) sulfur and oxygen isotopic stratigraphy of Devonian ; 4 ) integrated stratigraphy studies on the Devonian System in other stratigraphic regions except South China region . <p> Disclaimer : AAAS and EurekAlert ! are not responsible for the accuracy of news releases posted to EurekAlert ! by contributing institutions or for the use of any information through the EurekAlert system . <h> More on this News Release <p> Strategic Priority Research Program of Chinese Academy of Sciences , National Natural Science Foundation of China , Special Program for Basic Research of the Ministry of Science and Techology of @ @ @ @

@@70244709 <h> Our view : Getting rid of the rat pack <p> We 're not talking about stool pigeons in the mob movies of old but the long-tailed rodents who are increasingly skittering across yards , driveways and basements across the North Shore . <p> No one is quite sure of the reason for the influx . Some point to the recent spate of development across the region -- all that blasting and digging is pushing the rodents out of the shadows and into our backyards . The building boom has meant more dumpsters and trash receptacles where the animals can find a ready meal . Others point to climate change -- warmer temperatures and milder winters mean the rats may reproduce more often . And more often is a relative term : A mother rat can have up to 14 babies , and that 's after a gestation period of a mere two weeks . <p> " You take one pregnant rat and you come back in one year , and all of the descendants of that pregnant rat will have become 15,000 to 18,000 rats , " rodentologist ( yes , it 's a thing ) Bobby Corrigan @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ residents are freaking out . <p> In Peabody , for example , rat complaints rose from 23 in 2016 to 103 in 2017 , according to Health Director Sharon Cameron . @@70246555 <h> Share this story <p> Cities often see flash floods get worse as urbanization grows , as a cityscape is an incredibly efficient rainwater collector . The more land you pave , the more rain turns to surface runoff instead of soaking into the ground . If an area is connected by storm sewers , a lot of runoff can quickly come together in the same spot and pile up inconveniently . <p> A hurricane is no ordinary rainstorm , but the same problem applies . After Hurricane Harvey released an incredible amount of water on Houston last year , every aspect of the storm was dissected by public discussion and scientific studies . Researchers have concluded that climate change very likely played a role in Harvey 's record-setting rainfall , for example . <h> Further Reading <p> As for Houston 's rapid growth and development , attention has mostly focused on decisions to allow construction in risky , flood-prone areas . But a new study led by Wei Zhang and Gabriele Villarini of the University of Iowa has identified another impact beyond catching more of the rain with concrete -- Houston actually increasedthe rainfall itself . <p> It @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ surrounding area as all that pavement heats up in the Sun . This warm air rises , where it can cool and wring out its moisture as rain ; researchers have studied this weather influence in some cities in earlier studies . <p> In this case , the researchers wanted to see if something similar could apply to a hurricane like Harvey . So they simulated Harvey with a computer model , swapping out the urban area of Houston for farmland in some simulations . The model used the actual temperature patterns from the days before the hurricane , allowing it to simulate a storm that behaved just like Harvey did . <h> Further Reading <p> The results showed that a bigger Houston coaxed more rainfall out of the storm -- several more inches of rain , in fact . It also shifted the location of the most intense rain to the east side of the city . <p> How could that happen ? By examining the model carefully , the researchers found that warmer surface temperatures helped , but it had more to do with the city interacting with @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ any fluid , and the atmosphere is no different . Here , the extra drag the city 's buildings caused at the surface resulted in a little bit of a traffic jam , pushing air upward . And that upward boost means more water vapor turns to raindrops . <p> Another way to describe the extra rainfall is to calculate the changed probability of the Harvey flooding . Scaling actual stream channel records using the Harvey storm simulations , the researchers find that Houston 's development increased the odds of extreme flooding from rains produced by the storm by an incredible factor of 21 over what it would have been in 1950 . As unlikely an event as Harvey was , that magnitude of flooding would have been even more rare if Houston had n't grown explosively . <p> Natural disasters with human impacts are often not just " natural . Reforming the law such that utilities would pay damages only in cases of proven negligence would take a lot of the financial risk off the companies and transfer it to homeowners ( and their insurance companies @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ inverse condemnation . " Under inverse , energy companies face massive , essentially uninsurable risks , even when they have followed established safety and compliance rules , " said PG&amp;E 's Robison . <p> With fire costs surging in recent years , it 's not hard to imagine a fire big enough to take PG&amp;E under . Insurers paid out $4.2 billion for insured losses caused by California fires in 2016 , according to a report by A.M. Best . In 2017 insured losses from U.S. wildfires ballooned to $16 billion -- the only year globally that fire losses have surpassed $10 billion , according to Greg Heerde , head of analytics at insurance brokerage Aon Benfield . With $600 billion of available capital at re/insurance companies , the industry can handle the claims for now . <p> But insurance companies are having to reassess how they price coverage in California . With 45 of 58 counties seeing population growth since 2012 ; 12 of the past 19 years bringing below-average rain and snow ; an onslaught of tree-killing insects ; and longer fire seasons -- the threat of catastrophic @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ fire behavior , extended fire seasons and evolving weather and climate conditions are only creating greater need for adaptation , " says Heerde . <p> The number of acres burned this year is already twice that of 2017 , when about 9,000 structures were reduced to ashes . Insured losses in the Camp Fire could be even higher than early expectations , according to A.M. Best , because last year 's fires have already created a shortage of construction labor in the region , thus boosting the replacement cost of many charred homes in Paradise . <p> Without the utility companies to go after for compensation , home insurers will inevitably hike the cost of fire coverage to more adequately reflect the risks . And while it hardly seems fair to shift the liability burden from the utility to homeowners and insurers , the Wharton group explains that " the utility does not have control over many important drivers of wildfire risk , such as weather conditions , land use decisions , and building codes . " Though it 's essential that utilities take " cost-effective " precautions against fires @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ conditions beyond their control ( like climate change ) , it would result in lowered credit ratings , fewer profits , tougher financing , and ultimately , less reliable electric service for all Californians . " To be clear , there is no free pass , " says Robison . " Anyone harmed by the tragic wildfires can still pursue a negligence claim against PG&amp;E. "
